text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- It is very important to keep the world's attention on Bosnia, Moslem co-chairman in the Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic said after meeting with U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum.

- International committee and arbitration commission for disputed northern Bosnian town Brcko have historical responsibility in deciding town's fate, Moslem-Croat Federation vice-president Ejup Ganic says at meeting in Rome.
- Brcko should be given to its residents who lived there according to 1991 census, said leader of the Serb Civic Council Mirko Pejanovic, Serb group politically active in the Moslem-Croat Federation.

- Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic and Croat member of the presidency Kresimir Zubak meet in Sarajevo with two U.S. senators Carl Levin and Jack Reed to discuss current political situation in Bosnia.
- Our expectations are completely fulfilled, Bosnian foreign trade minister Hasan Muratovic says after information donors' conference in Brussels last week.

- Non-Serb residents in Bosnian Serb entity have hardly any basic human rights and even Serbs are having problems, Branko Todorovic, president of Helsinki committee for human rights chapter in Bijeljina in Serb republic, says in interview.
- Bosnia's economic potential has been cut to 10 or 15 percent of pre-war level during the 43-month war, Moslem-Croat federation agriculture minister Ahmed Smajic says in interview.

- Bosnian Serb delegation at Rome arbitration meeting over town of Brcko offers secret deal to the Moslem-Croat federation if it gives up hearing, newspaper quotes sources as saying. Bosnian official says it was only a media game in which the Serbs wanted to score a point.
- Number of policemen in Moslem-Croat Federation will be cut by 30 percent and 5,000 of them will be laid off, federation interior minister Mehmed Zilic tells local TV.

- Three unidentified persons attacked Bosnian government official and his driver on Bosnian Croat-controlled road in southern Bosnia on Saturday, pointed their guns at them and taking all their money.
- Dayton peace agreement is in crisis and there has been no political will to implement it from the very beginning, member of Dayton expert team Kasim Begic says in interview.
